theater: 維拉克魯斯與墨西哥灣沿岸

battle.name: 法摩戰爭
battle.theater: 維拉克魯斯與墨西哥灣沿岸
battle.brief: 1844 年 11 月，法國海軍遠征分艦隊再度駛入墨西哥灣，封鎖維拉克魯斯等港口，追討 1839 年和約未付的 60 萬比索賠款。墨方以沿岸砲台、海軍巡邏與民兵應戰，雙方在維拉克魯斯外海零星交火，衝突延續到 1845 年，最後以外交折衷收場。雷管步槍是守軍在城牆後的射手武器。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰雙方是法國王國與墨西哥共和國，但力量的分配一邊在海上、一邊在岸上。法國一方以海軍遠征分艦隊為主，旗艦與分遣隊由海軍少將夏爾·博丹率領——正是 1838 至 1839 年封鎖墨西哥灣的第一位指揮官；分艦隊包含巡防艦、砲艦、汽船與運輸船，岸戰由海軍陸戰隊步兵配合工程與醫療人員，艦上火炮擔任壓制港口與砲位的主要火力。巴黎方面由國王路易-菲利普主持，總理兼外長基佐主導外交，對墨西哥的索償文書經駐墨西哥公使與法國商會遞交。墨西哥一方是共和國中央政府、海軍與沿岸守軍：1844 年上半年由總統曼努埃爾·米切爾特雷納主持，同年 11 月夸爾納瓦科計畫之後聖安納回國，與內政部長馬里亞諾·奧特羅、戰爭部長佩德羅·馬里亞·阿納亞組成三頭政府，財政與海防由戰爭部與財政部分擔。海軍方面只得以數艘護衛艦與新購的蒸汽輪機船拼湊，守備維拉克魯斯與坦皮科的砲台、城防營和民兵。英國在墨西哥灣的商船最多，希望航路照開；美國海軍在得克薩斯沿岸監視法國船隻，這兩種立場決定了衝突會以封鎖、扣船、談判的方式收場。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Kingdom of France and the Mexican Republic, but their strength was distributed on opposite sides of the water: one had it afloat, the other ashore. On the French side the instrument was an expeditionary squadron of the navy, its flag and detachments led by Rear Admiral Charles Baudin — the very officer who had commanded the first blockade of the Gulf of Mexico in 1838 and 1839. The squadron mixed frigates, gunvessels, steamers and transports, and the fighting on land was carried by marine infantry supported by engineers and medical staff, while the ships' guns supplied the heavy fire that kept the port and its batteries under pressure. In Paris the king was Louis-Philippe, and the foreign ministry was in the hands of the prime minister and foreign minister Guizot; the claims against Mexico were presented through the French legation in Mexico City and through the French chambers of commerce. On the Mexican side stood the central government of the republic, the navy and the coastal garrisons. The first half of 1844 was conducted under the president Manuel Micheltorena; after the Plan of Cuernavaco of November that year Santa Anna came home and formed a triumvirate with the interior minister Mariano Otero and the war minister Pedro María Anaya, and the war and finance ministries between them carried the cost of coastal defence. The navy could only scrape together a few frigates and newly acquired steam vessels, and the defence of Veracruz and Tampico rested on fixed batteries, garrison troops and local militia. Britain had the largest merchant fleet in the Gulf and wanted the sea lanes kept open; the United States navy watched French ships from the Texan coast. Those two positions decided that the conflict would be settled by blockade, seizure and negotiation rather than by invasion.
people: 關鍵人物集中在三處。巴黎的兩位：路易-菲利普與基佐，前者要的是國威與貿易，後者把對墨西哥施壓當成外交籌算，願意批准分艦隊出航。海上的夏爾·博丹，1838 至 1839 年的經驗讓他直接沿用封鎖線與奪港辦法，重視速度與突然，不願把兵力散在陸上。墨西哥城的聖安納，1844 年底結束流亡返國，在夸爾納瓦科計畫推動下重掌政府，主張以沿岸防禦與談判並用，避免在城外與法軍分艦隊正面決鬥；戰爭部長佩德羅·馬里亞·阿納亞掌管軍費與海軍購置，是推動添置蒸汽輪機船、修整維拉克魯斯砲位的人；內政部長馬里亞諾·奧特羅處理外國商人的請願與索償清單。維拉克魯斯與坦皮科方面，當地民兵指揮官與海軍岸防分隊指揮官負責徵召民團、封鎖海灘、監視走私船隻。英國在墨西哥灣的巡航艦隊與美國海軍在得克薩斯的分遣隊，同樣是這段歷史的參與者：前者避免為法國封鎖線護航，後者盯住法國船隻往來。1844 年的接觸規模細小，多數決策是在數百公里外的港口與宮廷之間作出。
peopleEn: The decisive figures sat in three places. In Paris there were Louis-Philippe and Guizot: the king wanted prestige and trade, while the minister was ready to treat pressure on Mexico as a diplomatic instrument and to sanction the squadron's departure. At sea stood Charles Baudin, whose experience of 1838 and 1839 had taught him to reuse the blockade line and the seizure of the port, valuing speed and surprise and unwilling to scatter his strength ashore. In Mexico City there was Antonio López de Santa Anna, who came back from exile at the end of 1844 and regained the government in the wake of the Plan of Cuernavaco; he favoured coastal defence and negotiation together, and was unwilling to risk a set-piece battle outside the walls against a French squadron. The war minister Pedro María Anaya handled the military budget and the purchase of naval vessels, and was the man behind acquiring steamers and refitting the Veracruz batteries. The interior minister Mariano Otero worked through the compensation claims filed by foreign merchants. At Veracruz and Tampico, local militia commanders and shore-defence captains of the navy were responsible for calling out the townsmen, closing the beaches and watching the smuggling craft. The British cruising squadron in the Gulf and the American naval detachment off Texas were participants as well: the first declined to convoy French blockade runners, the second kept an eye on French shipping. The contacts of 1844 were small in scale, and most decisions were taken in ports and in palaces hundreds of kilometres apart.
kits: 兵器上這場衝突的主軸是海軍：法國巡防艦與砲艦把炮口對準維拉克魯斯外海，墨西哥能倚仗的是固定砲台與要塞。步槍方面，法國陸軍與海軍陸戰隊在一八四〇年前後完成雷管換裝，雷管步槍以可擊發底火取代火燧與火繩，霧天、拂曉與夜間不必再擔心引火失誤，槍口白煙與火焰也少，列陣射擊的節奏得以維持；法軍以銅帽雷管配合卡紙槍帶與圓彈，裝藥按口徑調整，連發速度高於舊式燧發槍。海軍陸戰隊的登陸分隊常以數十人為一隊，配步槍、刺刀與少量手槍，在灘頭與城牆缺口以射速壓制守軍。分艦隊同時攜帶艦載二十四磅砲與砲艦速射砲，用於遠距離打擊港口建築與砲位。墨西哥軍隊的步槍以德國製燧發槍為主，1840 年代起部分改裝雷管，槍管較短、彈道偏弱；志願民兵與城防營多為老舊槍械，補充不易。全程沒有攻城重炮，沒有裝甲，也沒有鐵路，只有帆船、蒸汽輪機船、艦載砲與固定砲台在對峙。
kitsEn: The main axis of this conflict was naval: French frigates and gunvessels trained their guns on the roads off Veracruz, and all Mexico could rely on was fixed batteries and the old fortress. As for shoulder arms, the French army and the marine infantry completed their percussion conversion around 1840; the percussion rifle replaced the flint and the match with a hammer-struck primer, so that in fog, at dawn and at night the troops no longer had to fear a misfire, the white smoke and the flash at the muzzle diminished, and the rhythm of linear volleys could be sustained. The French used a copper cap with a paper cartridge and a round ball, the charge adjusted to the calibre, and their rate of fire was higher than that of the older flint muskets. Landing detachments of the marines commonly went ashore in parties of a few dozen, with rifle, bayonet and a few pistols, and they used their rate of fire to pin the defenders at the beaches and at the breaches in the wall. The squadron carried its ships' twenty-four pounders and the quick-firing guns of the gunvessels for long-range fire against port buildings and battery positions. The Mexican army's muskets were mainly German-made flint pieces, with some converted to percussion during the 1840s, shorter in barrel and weak in trajectory; the volunteer militia and the garrison battalions were largely armed with old weapons that were hard to replace. There was no heavy siege artillery, no armour and no railway in the whole affair — only sailing ships, steamers, shipborne guns and fixed batteries stood against each other.
tactics: 法國的戰法是封鎖加奪港，不求速戰。分艦隊沿墨西哥灣海岸巡弋，攔截商船、扣押貨物、徵用港內船塢與海關倉庫，切斷維拉克魯斯這座全國主要外稅口岸的收入，讓墨西哥政府的現金流斷裂；登陸分隊以數百人規模突入要塞與碼頭區，控制砲位與旗桿，逼迫墨西哥坐到談判桌前。防守方採取三道線：外海由海軍巡邏艦與武裝走私船對峙，攔截法國登陸艇；海灘與碼頭由民兵與城防營挖壕、堆胸牆、埋地雷；城牆與砲台內由正規營擔任，壓制登陸點與停泊位。1840 年代法國海軍已用蒸汽輪機艦巡弋，能脫離風向獨立航行，封鎖線不必靠帆船排成一線維持。墨方避免重演 1838 年那樣在城牆外與法軍正面對射的風險，多以夜襲與游擊消耗登陸分隊，寧可讓出灘頭也不肯丟掉砲位。雙方都沒有把衝突升級為地面大會戰：法軍兵力不足以攻佔城市與廣大內陸，墨方則怕一場敗仗牽動港口與關稅，最後由外交回合收拾。
tacticsEn: French method was blockade plus seizure of the port, not a quick decision. The squadron cruised along the Mexican Gulf coast, stopping merchantmen, seizing cargo, taking over the shipyards and customs warehouses inside the harbour, and cutting the revenue of Veracruz, the country's main port for foreign customs, so that the Mexican government's cash flow was broken. Landing detachments of several hundred men pushed into the fortress and the dock area, took over the batteries and the flagstaff, and forced Mexico to the negotiating table. The defence was arranged in three lines: on the open water, navy patrol vessels and armed smuggling boats sparred with the French and contested their landing craft; on the beach and the quays, militia and garrison battalions dug trenches, threw up breastworks and planted mines; inside the walls and the batteries, regular battalions covered the landing places and the anchorages. In the 1840s the French navy already cruised with steamers that could hold their course independently of the wind, so the blockade line no longer had to be maintained by frigates in line ahead. Mexico avoided repeating the risk of 1838, when the garrison fought the French in the open outside the walls, and preferred night attacks and harassment to wear down the landing parties, giving up the beach rather than the batteries. Neither side escalated the affair into a great land battle: the French had not the strength to take the cities and the interior, while Mexico feared that one defeat would cost it the port and the customs revenue, and the outcome was settled in the diplomatic chamber instead.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。1839 年 3 月 9 日的和約規定墨西哥向法國支付 60 萬比索、折約 300 萬法郎，作為法國公民財產損失的賠償，這筆錢從未支付，成為 1844 年再度動武的直接理由。法國在 1830 年代是墨西哥第三大貿易夥伴，卻未取得與美國、英國類似的低關稅與引港條約。韋拉克魯斯至墨西哥城的公路距離約 300 公里，沿海岸自韋拉克魯斯至坦皮科約 500 公里的港口線都在封鎖之下；韋拉克魯斯城人口約一萬，墨西哥城約十二萬至十五萬。1844 年墨西哥海軍可用船艇以數艘護衛艦與蒸汽輪機船計，遠少於法國遠征分艦隊的巡防艦與砲艦。交火本身規模細小，多為單艦對岸砲、登陸分隊與民兵之間的零星接觸，法軍沒有投入一個旅以上的地面部隊，雙方也沒有留下可比的傷亡數字。封鎖期間，維拉克魯斯與坦皮科的進港船隻明顯減少，走私多沿尤卡坦與塔巴斯科的小港進行，這是航線上看得見的變化。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The treaty of 9 March 1839 had laid down that Mexico should pay France 600,000 pesos, about 3 million francs, as compensation for the loss of French citizens' property; the money was never paid, and that unpaid sum became the immediate ground for the resort to force in 1844. Through the 1830s France was Mexico's third largest trading partner, yet it had obtained no low-tariff or port-favoured treaties of the kind enjoyed by the United States and Britain. The road distance from Veracruz to Mexico City is about 300 kilometres, and some 500 kilometres of coast line, from Veracruz to Tampico, lay under blockade; the town of Veracruz counted roughly ten thousand inhabitants, while Mexico City counted something between one hundred and thirty thousand and one hundred and fifty thousand. The Mexican navy could put to sea only a few frigates and steamers in 1844, far fewer than the frigates and gunvessels of the French expeditionary squadron. The fighting itself was small in scale, consisting mostly of isolated exchanges between a single ship and the shore batteries, and between landing parties and the militia; the French never committed more than a brigade on land, and neither side left behind casualty figures that can be compared. During the blockade the number of vessels entering Veracruz and Tampico fell sharply, while smuggling shifted to the small harbours of Yucatán and Tabasco, a change plainly visible in the shipping movements.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。第一層是舊帳未清：1838 至 1839 年封鎖戰之後，條約上的 60 萬比索分文未付，法國商人、傳教士與在墨公民的申損名單仍在增加，巴黎把這視為國家信用的問題。第二層是貿易利益：法國商船在墨西哥對外貿易中居第三位，卻拿不到美英那樣的關稅與港口特惠，基佐內閣想用壓力換取條約，港口封鎖是最省兵力的手段。第三層是墨西哥的內部動盪：地方派系鬥爭與盜匪使外國人財產受損卻無從申訴，法國便以護衛本國國民的名義介入。同時英國在墨西哥灣的商船最多，不願看到封鎖升級成戰爭，便在背後推動折衷；美國海軍在得克薩斯沿岸盯住法國船隻，也讓巴黎不敢在陸地投入太多兵力，維持封鎖、施壓、談判的節奏。墨西哥政府當時也明白，英國的商船佔墨西哥對外貿易的大宗，若與法國正面開戰而英國倒向墨方，港口與鄉間都會受牽連。
causeEn: There were three layers behind the fighting. The first was the old unpaid account: after the blockade war of 1838 and 1839 not a peso of the sum agreed in the treaty had been paid, the list of losses claimed by French merchants, missionaries and citizens resident in Mexico kept growing, and Paris treated the matter as a question of national credit. The second was trade: French shipping ranked third in Mexico's foreign trade yet received neither the tariff concessions nor the port privileges held by the Americans and the British, and Guizot's cabinet wanted to use pressure to obtain a treaty, a blockade of the ports being the cheapest way to apply that pressure. The third was the internal disorder of Mexico, where factional fighting and banditry destroyed the property of foreigners without any means of redress, so France intervened under the banner of protecting its own nationals. At the same time Britain, with the largest merchant fleet in the Gulf, was unwilling to see the blockade escalate into a war and quietly promoted a compromise, while the United States navy, watching French shipping off the Texan coast, kept Paris from committing many troops on land and held it to the rhythm of blockade, pressure and negotiation. The Mexican government was also aware that British shipping accounted for a large share of Mexico's foreign trade; had Britain taken Mexico's side in a full war, both the ports and the countryside would have been dragged into it.
impact: 這場衝突沒有改變墨西哥的版圖，影響卻沿幾條線延伸。第一，法國確立了以海軍封鎖施壓的辦法，此後對墨西哥的索償都建立在 1839 年那筆未付賠款之上，這條理由一直被人引用，成為一八六〇年代法國再度干涉墨西哥時最常被提起的藉口。第二，墨西哥的沿岸防禦體系因這幾年經驗而固定下來：維拉克魯斯與坦皮科的砲台編制、海軍巡邏與民兵徵召辦法，後來在一八六二年法軍登陸時仍是可用的骨架。第三，經濟上，連續封鎖打斷港口收入，墨西哥財政更依賴英美貸款，法墨關係長期冷淡。第四，一般認為法國在墨西哥的商業與土地利益與美國在得克薩斯的爭端，最終在一八四六年美墨戰爭中爆發；封鎖、索償與得克薩斯地契被視為那場戰爭的遠因之一。對法國而言，這一場沒有贏家，只換來一次談判的教訓：索償要靠封鎖施壓，而封鎖要靠實力與外交同時運作。
impactEn: The conflict changed no borders, but its effects ran along several lines. First, France settled on the method of applying pressure by naval blockade, and every later claim against Mexico was built on the unpaid indemnity of 1839; that ground was cited repeatedly and became the most frequently advanced justification when France intervened in Mexico again in the 1860s. Second, Mexico's coastal defence system was fixed by the experience of those years: the battery organisation at Veracruz and Tampico, the patrol work of the navy and the calling up of the militia were still the working skeleton when French troops landed in 1862. Third, economically, repeated blockades cut the revenue of the ports, the Mexican treasury came to lean on British and American loans, and relations between the two countries stayed cold for a long time. Fourth, it is generally held that French commercial and territorial interests in Mexico collided with the American quarrel over Texas and finally came to war in the Mexican-American War of 1846; the blockade, the compensation claims and the Texan land titles are all treated as distant causes of that war. For France the war brought no victory but a lesson: claims had to be enforced by blockade, and a blockade needed strength and diplomacy at once.
result: 打到什麼收場：法國沒有攻下整個國家，墨方也沒有把法軍趕出墨西哥灣。衝突延續到 1845 年，雙方以外交折衷收場，墨西哥承諾分期支付部分賠款並處理個別索償個案，法國解除封鎖、撤回分艦隊，兩國之間沒有留下正式宣戰的長期敵對，也沒有地面大會戰的勝負可記。墨軍在守禦中保住了維拉克魯斯這座外稅港與主要砲位，海軍也第一次靠蒸汽輪機船在灣內維持巡航，這些經驗後來被不斷引用。戰爭之後，墨西哥與法國的關係並未斷裂，但索償的帳一直沒有清；法國的注意力轉向歐洲事務，墨方則把海防與財政的漏洞帶進一八四六年的危機，最終在北方丟掉大片領土。整體而言，墨西哥保住了領土與主要港口，法國則保住了自己在墨西哥的貿易位置與索償權，兩邊都沒有取得決定性的優勢。
resultEn: This is how it ended: France did not conquer the country, and Mexico did not drive the French out of the Gulf. The conflict ran into 1845 and was closed by a diplomatic compromise — Mexico undertook to pay part of the compensation in instalments and to settle individual claims, France lifted the blockade and recalled the squadron, and no lasting state of war left over from a formal declaration survived between the two countries, nor was there any great land battle whose outcome could be recorded. In the defence the Mexican army kept Veracruz, that port of customs, and its principal batteries, and the navy for the first time maintained a cruising presence in the Gulf on steamers; these lessons were quoted again and again afterwards. The war left relations between Mexico and France unbroken, but the account of compensation was never closed: French attention turned to affairs in Europe, while Mexico carried the gaps in its coastal defence and its finances into the crisis of 1846, and there it lost large tracts of its northern territory. In the end Mexico kept its territory and its principal ports, France kept its trading position in Mexico and its right to press its claims, and neither side gained a decisive advantage.
